examples.ko: 주말이라 시장에 사람들이 바글바글 모여 있어요.
examples.en: It's the weekend, so the market is swarming with people.
The soup is bubbling away in the pot.
It's vacation, so the amusement park is packed with kids.

examples.ko: 수족관 안에 작은 물고기가 바글바글 헤엄쳐요.
examples.en: Lots of little fish are swarming around in the aquarium.

examples.ko: 퇴근 시간에는 지하철역이 사람들로 바글바글해서 걷기 힘들어요.
examples.en: At rush hour the subway station is so crowded that it's hard to walk.

examples.ko: 벌레가 바글바글 있는 걸 보고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled to see bugs crawling all over in huge numbers.

explain: 사람이나 벌레, 물고기처럼 많은 것이 한곳에 모여 움직일 때 써요. 국이나 물이 끓는 모습에도 쓰는데, 이때는 '보글보글'과 비슷한 느낌이에요. '바글바글하다'로도 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when many people, bugs or fish crowd into one place and keep moving. It also describes liquid boiling, where it feels close to '보글보글'. You can also say '바글바글하다'.

examples.ko: 우리 바깥양반은 오늘 회사에서 늦게 와요.
examples.en: My husband will come home late from work today.
Is your husband doing well these days?
If your husband is home, please come together.
My husband likes kimchi stew the best.

examples.ko: 옆집 아주머니가 바깥양반 자랑을 한참 했어요.
examples.en: The lady next door bragged about her husband for a long time.
I'll ask my husband and get back to you.

explain: 나이 드신 분들이 자기 남편을 남에게 말하거나, 남의 남편을 높여 부를 때 써요. 젊은 사람들은 보통 '남편'이라고 해요. 짝이 되는 말은 '안사람'이에요.
explain_en: Older speakers use it for their own husband when talking to others, or to refer politely to someone else's husband. Younger people usually just say '남편'. Its counterpart is '안사람' (wife).

examples.en: Every evening my grandmother sits down with her sewing.
The sewing has piled up, so I plan to do it all at once on the weekend.

examples.ko: 어머니가 바느질감을 한 보따리 들고 오셨어요.
examples.en: My mother came carrying a big bundle of sewing.
This piece only needs the buttons sewn on and it's done.
She is dozing with her sewing on her lap.

examples.ko: 가방에 바느질감을 넣어 다니면서 틈틈이 해요.
examples.en: I carry my sewing in my bag and work on it whenever I have time.

explain: 바느질할 옷이나 천을 가리켜요. '바느질'은 하는 일이고, '바느질감'은 그 일을 할 물건이에요. 보통 '바느질감을 꺼내다, 바느질감이 쌓이다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to the clothes or fabric you are going to sew. '바느질' is the activity, while '바느질감' is the material for it. You will often hear '바느질감을 꺼내다' or '바느질감이 쌓이다'.

examples.ko: 바늘귀가 너무 작아서 실이 안 들어가요.
examples.en: The eye of the needle is so small that the thread won't go in.

examples.ko: 눈이 나빠서 바늘귀에 실을 꿰기 힘들어요.
examples.en: My eyesight is bad, so it's hard to thread the needle.
Please switch to a needle with a bigger eye.

examples.ko: 할머니가 바늘귀에 실을 꿰 달라고 부탁하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother asked me to thread the needle for her.
The thread keeps slipping out of the needle's eye.
I couldn't find the needle's eye, so I turned on the light.

explain: 몸의 귀가 아니라 바늘에서 실을 꿰는 작은 구멍을 말해요. '바늘귀에 실을 꿰다'처럼 '꿰다'와 함께 자주 써요.
explain_en: This is not the ear on your body; it is the small hole in a needle where the thread goes. It is often used with '꿰다', as in '바늘귀에 실을 꿰다'.

examples.en: The stitches in this embroidery are really delicate.
The stitches weren't even, so I sewed it again.
If you make the stitches small, the clothes are sturdier.
With hand sewing, care goes into every single stitch.

examples.ko: 바늘땀 사이가 너무 넓으면 금방 뜯어져요.
examples.en: If the gaps between stitches are too wide, it comes apart quickly.

examples.ko: 바늘땀이 보이지 않게 안쪽에서 꿰매 주세요.
examples.en: Please sew it from the inside so the stitches don't show.

explain: 바늘로 한 번 떠서 남은 자국 하나를 말해요. 줄여서 '땀'이라고도 하고, 손으로 정성껏 할 때 '한 땀 한 땀'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is the single mark left each time the needle goes through the cloth. People shorten it to '땀', and say '한 땀 한 땀' for careful hand work.

examples.ko: 시험 결과를 기다리는 동안 바늘방석에 앉은 기분이었어요.
examples.en: While waiting for my test results, I felt like I was sitting on pins and needles.
I sat next to my boss, so the whole meeting was agony.
My grandmother keeps her needles stuck in a pin cushion.

examples.ko: 다들 아는 사실을 나만 몰라서 바늘방석 같았어요.
examples.en: Everyone knew but me, so I felt awfully uncomfortable.
I don't know where I put the pin cushion.

examples.ko: 그 자리는 정말 바늘방석이라 얼른 나오고 싶었어요.
examples.en: That seat was so uncomfortable that I wanted to leave right away.

explain: 바늘을 꽂아 두는 물건이지만, 대화에서는 마음이 불편하고 불안한 자리를 비유할 때 더 많이 나와요. 보통 '바늘방석에 앉다, 바늘방석 같다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 면접 내내 바늘방석에 앉은 것처럼 불안했어요.
phrases.en: to feel very uneasy in a situation
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 앉는 것이 아니라 불안하고 불편한 상황에 있을 때 써요. '바늘방석에 앉은 기분'이라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: You are not literally sitting; it describes being in an anxious, uncomfortable situation. People also say '바늘방석에 앉은 기분'.
phrases.en_equiv: be on pins and needles; feel like squirming in one's seat

explain_en: It is literally a pin cushion, but in conversation it is often used figuratively for a seat or situation where you feel uneasy. It usually appears as '바늘방석에 앉다' or '바늘방석 같다'.

examples.ko: 아기가 기저귀를 갈 때 다리를 바동거려요.
examples.en: The baby kicks and wriggles his legs when I change his diaper.

examples.ko: 잡힌 벌레가 손 안에서 바동거리고 있어요.
examples.en: The bug I caught is wriggling in my hand.

examples.ko: 물에 빠진 아이가 바동거리는 걸 보고 바로 뛰어들었어요.
examples.en: I saw the child flailing in the water and jumped in right away.
The child said he wouldn't go and kicked and squirmed on the floor.
The fish caught on the fishing line struggled until it was exhausted.
No matter how much you struggle like that, it's no use.

explain: 작은 몸이나 손발을 급하게 흔들며 벗어나려고 애쓰는 모습이에요. '버둥거리다'와 같은 계열로, '바동'이 더 작고 가벼운 느낌을 줘요. 어려운 상황에서 벗어나려고 애쓴다는 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It describes a small body or limbs moving quickly as someone tries to get free. It belongs to the same family as '버둥거리다', with '바동' feeling smaller and lighter. It can also be used figuratively for striving hard to escape a bad situation.

examples.en: The baby is crying and kicking his legs about.

examples.ko: 바둥바둥 아끼며 살아도 돈이 잘 안 모여요.
examples.en: Even though I struggle to save, money doesn't build up.
The fly caught in the spider web is struggling and squirming.
He worked desperately to pay off his debt.

examples.ko: 바둥바둥 애를 써도 일이 풀리지 않아요.
examples.en: No matter how hard I strain, things don't work out.
The child is wriggling around to be picked up.

explain: 팔다리를 작게 흔들며 애쓰는 모습을 말해요. 아기나 작은 동물 이야기뿐 아니라 '바둥바둥 살다'처럼 힘들게 노력하는 모습에도 써요. 약간 안쓰러운 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It shows small arms and legs moving as one tries hard. It is used for babies and small animals, and also for people working hard against difficulty, as in '바둥바둥 살다'. It carries a slightly pitiful feeling.

examples.ko: 동생은 자기 말이 맞다고 바득바득 우겨요.
examples.en: My younger brother stubbornly insists he is right.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 바득바득 돈을 받아 내겠다고 했어요.
examples.en: He said he would get the money back no matter what.
The child keeps pestering me to buy it.
Why are you so determined to win at all costs?

examples.ko: 제가 오지 말라고 했는데 친구가 바득바득 따라왔어요.
examples.en: I told my friend not to come, but he insisted on following me.

examples.ko: 바득바득 고집을 부려 봤자 달라지는 건 없어요.
examples.en: Stubbornly digging in your heels won't change anything.

explain: '우기다, 조르다, 고집을 부리다'처럼 끈질기게 밀어붙이는 말과 자주 써요. '악착같이'는 열심히 해내는 느낌으로도 쓰지만, '바득바득'은 억지를 부린다는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It pairs with words for pushing persistently, such as '우기다', '조르다' and '고집을 부리다'. '악착같이' can sound like admirable determination, but '바득바득' leans toward being unreasonably stubborn.

examples.en: I'm so cold that my whole body is shivering.

examples.ko: 강아지가 천둥 소리에 바들바들 떨고 있어요.
examples.en: The puppy is trembling at the sound of thunder.
My hands were shaking before the presentation.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 지팡이를 잡은 손을 바들바들 떠세요.
examples.en: My grandfather's hand holding the cane is trembling.

examples.ko: 겁이 나서 다리가 바들바들 떨려 못 걸었어요.
examples.en: I was so scared that my legs shook and I couldn't walk.

examples.ko: 바들바들 떨지 말고 심호흡을 해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't shake like that, try taking a deep breath.

explain: 주로 '떨다, 떨리다'와 함께 써요. '벌벌'이 더 널리 쓰이고, '바들바들'은 작고 가늘게 계속 떠는 느낌이에요. 추위, 무서움, 긴장, 힘이 없을 때 모두 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It mostly goes with '떨다' or '떨리다'. '벌벌' is more widely used, while '바들바들' suggests small, thin, continuous trembling. It fits cold, fear, nerves or weakness.

examples.en: The child suddenly screamed at the top of his voice.
He got angry and snapped back fiercely.
My younger sister cried, screaming her lungs out.
No matter how I coax him, he just keeps insisting fiercely.

examples.ko: 엄마한테 바락 화를 내고 나서 후회했어요.
examples.en: I lashed out at my mom and then regretted it.
It felt so unfair that I shouted out before I knew it.

explain: 갑자기 크게 소리 지르거나 대들 때 쓰는 말이에요. '바락 소리를 지르다, 바락 대들다, 바락 악을 쓰다'처럼 말해요. 같은 말을 반복한 '바락바락'도 써요.
explain_en: It describes suddenly shouting or lashing out. Typical phrases are '바락 소리를 지르다', '바락 대들다' and '바락 악을 쓰다'. The repeated form '바락바락' is also used.

examples.en: I forgot our plans yesterday and stood my friend up.
I'm really sorry for standing you up on the blind date yesterday.
I can't believe you stood me up, that's too much.

examples.ko: 또 바람맞힐 거면 미리 말해 줘요.
examples.en: If you're going to stand me up again, tell me in advance.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 저를 바람맞혀서 혼자 영화를 봤어요.
examples.en: He stood me up, so I watched the movie alone.
Who stood you up?

explain: 약속 장소에 안 나타나서 상대를 기다리게 할 때 써요. 당한 사람 입장에서는 '바람맞다'라고 해요. 친구, 연인, 소개팅처럼 사람과의 약속에 많이 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you fail to show up and leave the other person waiting. From the victim's side, the word is '바람맞다'. It is common for dates, blind dates and plans with friends.

examples.ko: 그 가게에는 손님인 척하는 바람잡이가 있었대요.
examples.en: They say that shop had a decoy pretending to be a customer.

examples.ko: 행사 시작 전에 바람잡이가 분위기를 띄웠어요.
examples.en: Before the event started, a warm-up person got the crowd excited.

examples.ko: 친구가 바람잡이 역할을 해 줘서 모임이 즐거웠어요.
examples.en: My friend livened things up, so the gathering was fun.
Did you call me over to use me as your shill?
There is always a shill next to a con artist.

examples.ko: 그는 노래 전에 웃긴 말을 하며 바람잡이를 했어요.
examples.en: Before the song, he cracked jokes to get the crowd going.

explain: 두 가지로 써요. 행사에서 분위기를 띄우는 사람이라는 중립적인 뜻이 있고, 손님인 척하며 다른 사람이 물건을 사게 만드는 사람이라는 부정적인 뜻도 있어요. 어느 쪽인지는 문장의 흐름으로 알 수 있어요.
explain_en: It has two uses: a neutral one for a person who gets a crowd excited at an event, and a negative one for a person who pretends to be a customer so others will buy. The context tells you which is meant.

examples.ko: 소비자 물가는 경제 상황을 보여 주는 바로미터예요.
examples.en: Consumer prices are a barometer of the economy.

examples.ko: 이번 선거 결과가 민심의 바로미터가 될 거예요.
examples.en: This election result will be a barometer of public opinion.
They say sleep and appetite are the barometer of health.

examples.ko: 아이의 표정은 기분을 알려 주는 바로미터예요.
examples.en: A child's expression is a barometer of his mood.

examples.ko: 가게 앞 줄 길이가 맛집의 바로미터라고 하더라고요.
examples.en: People say the length of the line in front of a shop is the barometer of a good restaurant.

examples.ko: 이 시험을 실력을 재는 바로미터로 삼아 보세요.
examples.en: Try using this test as a barometer of your skills.

explain: 원래는 기압을 재는 기구지만, 보통 '~의 바로미터'처럼 상태를 알려 주는 기준이라는 비유로 써요. '지표'나 '척도'와 비슷하고, '바로미터가 되다, 바로미터로 삼다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It originally means a pressure gauge, but it is usually used figuratively as '~의 바로미터', a sign that shows the state of something. It is similar to '지표' and '척도', and appears in '바로미터가 되다' or '바로미터로 삼다'.

examples.en: The wrong information was corrected belatedly.

examples.ko: 오랜 습관이 한 달 만에 바로잡혔어요.
examples.en: My long-standing habit was fixed in a month.
Once your posture is corrected, back pain decreases.
I'm glad the misunderstanding was cleared up through talking.
The bent wire doesn't straighten out easily.

examples.ko: 잘못이 바로잡힐 때까지 계속 요구할 거예요.
examples.en: I'll keep demanding it until the mistake is corrected.

explain: '바로잡다'의 피동형으로, 잘못이나 비뚤어진 것이 고쳐지는 결과에 초점이 있어요. 사람이 고치는 상황은 '바로잡다', 저절로 또는 누군가에 의해 고쳐지는 상황은 '바로잡히다'를 써요. 오류, 자세, 질서, 오해와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: This is the passive form of '바로잡다' and focuses on the result of something wrong being fixed. When someone fixes it, use '바로잡다'; when it gets fixed, use '바로잡히다'. It fits errors, posture, order and misunderstandings.

examples.en: I was so angry that my lips quivered.
My fingertips tremble on cold days.

examples.ko: 그는 분을 못 참고 바르르 몸을 떨었어요.
examples.en: He couldn't hold back his anger and shook all over.
The little bird fluttered its wings.
My eyelid kept twitching, so I went to the hospital.
My voice trembled at those words.

explain: 가볍고 빠르게 한 번 떠는 모습이에요. 계속 떠는 '바들바들'보다 짧게 떠는 느낌이고, 더 큰 느낌의 말은 '부르르'예요. 분노, 추위, 긴장에 모두 써요.
explain_en: It shows a light, quick tremble. It feels shorter than the continuous '바들바들', and '부르르' is its bigger, heavier counterpart. It is used for anger, cold and nerves.

examples.en: Tell me the truth, who did it?
The teacher said that if we tell the truth, we'll be forgiven.
I told my mom everything honestly and apologized.

examples.ko: 바른대로 말하면 저는 그 일을 몰랐어요.
examples.en: To tell the truth, I didn't know about that.
Don't lie, just come clean.

examples.ko: 그때 바른대로 말하지 못한 게 계속 마음에 걸려요.
examples.en: It still weighs on me that I couldn't tell the truth back then.

explain: '바른대로 말하다, 바른대로 대다, 바른대로 이르다'처럼 말하는 것과 함께 써요. '사실대로'와 비슷하지만 잘못을 캐묻거나 솔직하게 털어놓으라고 할 때 더 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It goes with speaking verbs, as in '바른대로 말하다', '바른대로 대다' and '바른대로 이르다'. It is close to '사실대로', but it is heard more when someone is pressing for the truth or urging a confession.

examples.en: My mother packed loads of side dishes for me.

examples.ko: 명절에 시골에서 선물을 바리바리 챙겨 왔어요.
examples.en: For the holiday, I brought back piles of gifts from the countryside.
I got on the subway lugging a mountain of bags.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 뭘 그렇게 바리바리 싸요?
examples.en: What are you packing so much of for the trip?

examples.ko: 할머니는 올 때마다 먹을 걸 바리바리 가져오세요.
examples.en: Every time my grandmother visits, she brings a huge amount of food.

examples.ko: 이삿날 친구가 간식을 바리바리 사 왔어요.
examples.en: On moving day, my friend came with armfuls of snacks.

explain: 짐이나 먹을 것을 많이 꾸려서 싸거나 들고 오는 모습이에요. '싸다, 챙기다, 들다, 가져오다'와 잘 어울려요. 가족이 정성스럽게 챙겨 주는 상황에 특히 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It shows someone packing or carrying a large amount of luggage or food. It goes well with '싸다', '챙기다', '들다' and '가져오다'. It often appears when family members generously prepare things for you.

examples.en: The police put up a barricade on the road.

examples.ko: 공사 구간 앞에 바리케이드가 세워져 있어요.
examples.en: A barricade has been set up in front of the construction section.

examples.ko: 바리케이드 때문에 차가 지나갈 수 없었어요.
examples.en: Cars couldn't get through because of the barricade.
They installed barricades on both sides of the road.
People are waiting in front of the barricade.
On festival days they block the street with barricades.

explain: 길이나 입구를 막아 놓은 구조물이에요. 공사, 행사, 사고 현장에서 볼 수 있고 '바리케이드를 치다, 설치하다'처럼 말해요. '바리게이트'라고 쓰는 사람도 있지만 표준 표기는 '바리케이드'예요.
explain_en: It is a structure set up to block a road or entrance, seen at construction sites, events and accident scenes. People say '바리케이드를 치다' or '설치하다'. Some write '바리게이트', but the standard spelling is '바리케이드'.

examples.en: My father sings the baritone part in the choir.
The baritone voice is deep and warm.
I took on a baritone role in an opera for the first time.
Baritone is more comfortable for me than tenor.

examples.ko: 이 곡은 바리톤을 위해 쓴 노래예요.
examples.en: This piece is a song written for baritone.
He is famous as a baritone singer.

explain: 남자 목소리 중 중간 높이의 음역, 또는 그 음역으로 노래하는 사람을 말해요. 높은 쪽은 '테너', 낮은 쪽은 '베이스'예요.
explain_en: It is the middle range of the male voice, or a singer in that range. The higher range is 'tenor' and the lower is 'bass'.

examples.en: I play the bassoon in the orchestra.
The sound of the bassoon is low and soft.

examples.ko: 동생이 학교 밴드에서 바순을 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is learning the bassoon in the school band.
In this piece, the bassoon carries the melody.
The bassoon is much bigger than the clarinet.
I want to become a bassoonist.

explain: 낮고 부드러운 소리를 내는 목관악기예요. '바순을 불다' 또는 '바순을 연주하다'라고 말해요. 오케스트라나 관악 합주에서 낮은 음을 맡을 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a woodwind instrument with a low, soft sound. You say '바순을 불다' or '바순을 연주하다'. In orchestras and wind ensembles it often covers the low parts.

examples.ko: 가방 안에서 비닐봉지가 바스락 소리를 내요.
examples.en: A plastic bag rustles inside my bag.

examples.ko: 낙엽을 밟을 때마다 바스락 소리가 나요.
examples.en: Every time I step on fallen leaves, there's a crunchy rustle.

examples.ko: 밤에 방에서 바스락 소리가 나서 깼어요.
examples.en: A rustling sound in my room at night woke me up.
The child rustled open the snack bag.
I can hear the rustle of paper being folded.

examples.ko: 이불 속에서 바스락 움직이는 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: There was a rustling sound of someone moving under the blanket.

explain: 마른 잎, 종이, 비닐 같은 것이 스치거나 움직일 때 나는 가벼운 소리예요. '바스락 소리가 나다'처럼 자주 쓰고, 더 크고 둔한 느낌의 말은 '부스럭'이에요.
explain_en: It is the light sound of dry leaves, paper or plastic brushing or moving. You often hear '바스락 소리가 나다'. The bigger, duller version is '부스럭'.

examples.en: The fallen leaves rustle in the wind.
The plastic bag keeps rustling and it bothers me.

examples.ko: 밤새 쥐가 바스락거리는 소리에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep because of a mouse rustling all night.

examples.ko: 마른 풀을 밟으면 바스락거리는 소리가 나요.
examples.en: When you step on dry grass, it makes a rustling sound.
The child played rustling around under the blanket.

examples.ko: 종이가 바스락거리지 않게 조심히 넘겨 주세요.
examples.en: Please turn the pages carefully so the paper doesn't rustle.

explain: '바스락' 소리가 계속 나거나 반복될 때 써요. '바스락'이 한 번 나는 소리라면 '바스락거리다'는 이어지는 소리예요. 밤에 방해되는 소리나 조용한 곳에서 들리는 작은 소리에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when the '바스락' sound continues or repeats. '바스락' is a single sound, while '바스락거리다' is an ongoing one. It often appears for small noises heard in a quiet place or at night.

examples.en: The old fallen leaf crumbled in my hand.

examples.ko: 쿠키를 가방에 넣었더니 다 바스러져 있었어요.
examples.en: I put the cookies in my bag, and they were all crumbled.
Dried petals crumble when you touch them.

examples.ko: 너무 오래된 종이라 손대면 바스러질 것 같아요.
examples.en: The paper is so old that it looks like it would crumble if touched.
The snack had crumbled, so it was awkward to eat.

examples.ko: 마른 흙이 바스러지는 느낌이 손에 남았어요.
examples.en: The feeling of dry soil crumbling stayed in my hand.

explain: '부서지다'보다 마르고 약한 것이 가루나 작은 조각으로 부서질 때 잘 어울려요. 낙엽, 과자, 마른 흙에 많이 쓰고, 더 큰 느낌의 말은 '부스러지다'예요.
explain_en: Compared with '부서지다', it fits dry, fragile things breaking into powder or small bits, such as leaves, snacks and dry soil. The bigger version is '부스러지다'.

en: at the height; on the verge of

examples.en: Spring is just now beginning.
A new era is just now opening up.
It is now the height of summer vacation season.
The moment we were waiting for has finally arrived.
This city is now in full festival mood.
Now is the time to announce the results.

explain: '이제 막, 지금 한창'이라는 느낌으로 문장 맨 앞에 자주 오는 글 느낌의 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '이제 곧, 드디어'가 더 자연스러워요. 계절이나 시대가 바뀌는 때를 말할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: It feels like 'right now, just at the point of', and often opens a sentence in a written or formal tone. In everyday talk '이제 곧' or '드디어' sounds more natural. It suits moments when a season or era is changing.

examples.en: My grandmother moves around busily from early morning.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 정말 바지런해서 일을 금방 끝내요.
examples.en: That friend is really diligent and finishes work quickly.

examples.ko: 바지런한 이웃 덕분에 골목이 늘 깨끗해요.
examples.en: Thanks to a diligent neighbor, the alley is always clean.

examples.ko: 동생은 바지런해서 쉬는 날에도 가만히 있지 않아요.
examples.en: My sibling is so industrious that he never sits still even on days off.
If you work diligently, the day goes by quickly.
My mother is industrious, so she even tends the garden herself.

explain: '부지런하다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 일을 미루지 않고 몸을 잘 움직이는 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요. 반대말은 '게으르다'예요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '부지런하다'. You use it to praise someone who doesn't put work off and keeps active. The opposite is '게으르다'.

examples.en: The baby looks so cute dressed in a baji-jeogori outfit.
The child's baji-jeogori got covered in dirt.
I had a set of baji-jeogori made at the hanbok shop.

examples.ko: 설날에 할아버지는 바지저고리 차림으로 세배를 받으셨어요.
examples.en: On New Year's Day, my grandfather received bows dressed in baji-jeogori.
I looked at old baji-jeogori at the museum.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 바지저고리가 흠뻑 젖어 버렸어요.
examples.en: My baji-jeogori got soaked on the rainy day.

explain: 한복의 바지와 저고리를 함께 부르는 말로, 주로 남자 한복 차림을 가리켜요. 사람에게 쓰면 줏대 없는 사람을 놀리는 말이 되니 조심하세요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 사장님 말만 듣는 바지저고리예요.
phrases.en: a spineless person who just does as told
phrases.nuance_ko: 한복 이름이 아니라 줏대 없이 시키는 대로만 하는 사람을 놀리는 말이에요. 듣는 사람 기분이 상할 수 있어서 직접 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here it isn't the clothing but a teasing label for someone who has no mind of their own and just follows orders. It can offend, so avoid saying it directly to someone.

explain_en: It names the trousers and jacket of hanbok together, mostly meaning the men's outfit. When applied to a person, it becomes a teasing way to call someone spineless, so be careful.
